title: Derived universal properties of supported scalar maps
statement: Let i : D → T be a closed immersion, let R and A be commutative rings, and let φ : R → A be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Suppose ηD and ηT are maps of the ordinary constant module sheaves [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] sending, at every étale object, each constant generator r to φ(r). Then ηD on D, ηT on T, and the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of ηD (transported through the objectwise restriction-of-scalars comparison) each satisfy the unbounded derived scalar-unit universal property [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-scalar]. No flatness of A is required.

proof.text: The affine description of a closed immersion gives $i^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}R=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. The $R$-module $R/I$ is generated by $1$, so $i$ is finite. A geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ has at most one lift to $D$: on this affine chart a lift is the unique factorization $R/I\to\Omega$, which exists exactly when $I$ maps to zero. This is exactly the condition that the image of $\bar t$ lies in $D$. Put $E=i_*\Lambda_D$. The finite stalk formula, with its restriction-of-germs normalization, and the constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism therefore give $E_{\bar t}=\Lambda$ on $D$ and $E_{\bar t}=0$ off $D$. The same computation gives $(i_*A_D)_{\bar t}=A$ or $0$. These are module identifications: the scalar action is restriction of constant coefficients, and the stated germ maps commute with multiplication by a constant.

proof.text: By finite direct-image exactness, $i_*$ is exact on abelian sheaves. It is also exact on sheaves of modules over either constant coefficient ring: kernels and cokernels carry their induced module structures and their underlying abelian sheaves are the abelian kernels and cokernels, so the same exact sequences are obtained after forgetting the action. Apply the exact-functor derived theorem. Thus $Ri_*\Lambda_D$ and $Ri_*A_D$ are canonically represented by $E[0]$ and $(i_*A_D)[0]$, and the comparison from ordinary to derived direct image is natural in the coefficient map and in the units.

We verify K-flatness of this particular $E[0]$ directly, without assuming flatness of $A$. Let $C^\bullet$ be any acyclic complex of $\Lambda_T$-modules. Since $E$ is in degree zero, the total tensor has degree $n$ term $C^n\otimes E$ and differential $d_C\otimes1$. Here $\otimes$ is the change-of-rings tensor over $\Lambda_T$, the sheafification of $U\mapsto C^n(U)\otimes_{\Lambda_T(U)}E(U)$, while the tensor-stalk comparison concerns the sheafification of $U\mapsto C^n(U)\otimes_\Lambda E(U)$. The surjection between these presheaves induces an isomorphism of sheafifications: on geometric stalks both are $C^n_{\bar t}\otimes_\Lambda E_{\bar t}$, because $(\Lambda_T)_{\bar t}=\Lambda$ by the constant-sheaf stalk isomorphism and filtered colimits commute with tensor products; conservativity then applies. The natural tensor-stalk comparison identifies its stalk complex with $C^\bullet_{\bar t}\otimes_\Lambda E_{\bar t}$, including differentials. Step 1 identifies this with $C^\bullet_{\bar t}$ or zero. Exactness of geometric stalks makes both complexes acyclic and identifies the stalk of each cohomology sheaf of $C^\bullet\otimes E$ with zero. Conservativity, applied to the map from that cohomology sheaf to zero, makes the sheaf zero. This is precisely the definition of K-flatness of $E[0]$. The identical argument with $\Lambda_T$ in place of $E$ shows that $\Lambda_T[0]$ is K-flat; all its stalks are $\Lambda$.

proof.text: Let $c:E\to i_*A_D$ be induced by $\Lambda_D\to A_D$. Define an $A_T$-linear map $m:E\otimes_{\Lambda_T}A_T\to i_*A_D$ as follows. On an etale $W\to T$, send a pure section tensor $s\otimes a$ to $c(s)\,a|_{W\times_TD}$. This is balanced over $\Lambda_T(W)$ and compatible with restriction, so the sheafified tensor universal property gives $m$. It is the unique $A_T$-linear extension of $c$, since $m(s\otimes1)=c(s)$ and pure tensors generate locally. This is the coefficient-adjunction comparison in the statement. At a geometric point on $D$, the germ formulas for tensor and finite direct image identify $m$ with $\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda A\to A$, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\lambda a$; its inverse is $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Off $D$ it is the map $0\to0$. Geometric-stalk conservativity therefore makes $m$ an isomorphism of sheaves of $A_T$-modules.

proof.text: Use the identity K-flat resolution $E[0]\to E[0]$ from step 3 in derived change of rings. Its canonical comparison represents $E[0]\otimes_{\Lambda_T}^{\mathbf L}A_T$ by $(E\otimes_{\Lambda_T}A_T)[0]$. Combining this with step 2 and the isomorphism $m$ of step 4 yields the required identification with $Ri_*A_D$. It is the specified comparison, not merely an abstract isomorphism: its ordinary representative is the unique coefficient-linear extension of $i_*(\Lambda_D\to A_D)$, and the K-flat computation is canonical and natural. No resolution of $A_T$, and no flatness of $A$ over $\Lambda$, has been used.
